title: Thermodynamics of words
abstract: arXiv:2611.14039v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We introduce the word thermalization hypothesis according to which in a literary work there are effective interactions between words that drive them to thermalization where their word frequency distribution is the same as for the phenomenon of Rayleigh-Jeans (RJ) thermalization and condensation. In this concept, the different words play a role of classical oscillators (particles) and their word frequencies, or related tokens, are analogous to certain filling factors over energy state levels. The thermalization process is characterized by the conservation of total system energy, or total number of words/tokens, and total probability norm, or total number of different words. We apply this approach to analyze 16 literary works, including Bible, complete works of Shakespeare, and data from American National Corpus. tldr: 该论文提出词汇热化假说，将文学作品中的词频分布类比为经典振荡器的瑞利-金斯热化与凝聚现象，并通过对《圣经》、莎士比亚全集等16部作品的分析，验证了低有效能量条件下会出现词汇的RJ凝聚。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a word thermalization hypothesis, modeling word frequency distributions in literary works as Rayleigh-Jeans thermalization and condensation of classical oscillators, and validates the low-energy RJ condensation phenomenon through analysis of 16 literary works including the Bible and Shakespeare's complete works.
